plan.chapterName: OpenStax Organic Chemistry, chapter 28: Biomolecules: Nucleic Acids
plan.contextChunk: This figure diagrams RNA transcription as a flat schematic of three nucleic acid strands drawn as tapered colored ribbons. A blue-violet ribbon runs across the top, labeled "DNA sense strand", marked 5' at its left tip and 3' at its right; a cyan ribbon runs along the bottom, labeled "DNA antisense strand", marked 3' at left and 5' at right. Both ribbons bow away from each other through the middle of the figure to open a bubble, and outside the bubble at each end their bases pair through vertical dot columns, C with G, A with T, and T with A at the left, G with C, A with T, and C with G at the right. Inside the bubble the sense strand's bases hang free and read T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T, while the antisense strand's exposed bases are hydrogen bonded to a magenta ribbon lying between the two, labeled "mRNA" by a leader line at its right end and marked 5' at left and 3' at right; its magenta bases read U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U. Placing the new transcript directly against its template makes the base-by-base complementarity readable in one glance, and comparing it upward with the blue-violet strand shows the two agree except that U stands wherever the sense strand carries T.

elements: DNA sense strand ribbon (blue-violet) running across the top, bowed upward through the central bubble, flat and close to the antisense strand in the left and right flanking regions
DNA antisense strand ribbon (cyan) running across the bottom, bowed downward through the bubble, flat in the flanks
mRNA ribbon (magenta) lying horizontally between the two DNA strands, present only inside the bubble, shorter than the DNA strands
5' and 3' end labels at the left and right tips of the sense strand (5' left, 3' right)
3' and 5' end labels at the left and right tips of the antisense strand (3' left, 5' right)
5' and 3' labels at the two ends of the mRNA (5' left, 3' right)
'DNA sense strand' text label with leader arrow at upper left
'DNA antisense strand' text label with leader arrow at lower left
'mRNA' text label with leader arrow at the right end of the magenta ribbon
sense-strand base letters hanging below the top ribbon inside the bubble: T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T
antisense-strand base letters rising above the bottom ribbon inside the bubble: A G T C G A C C G A C T T G C G C A A
mRNA base letters below the magenta ribbon inside the bubble: U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U
vertical dotted hydrogen-bond columns between antisense bases and mRNA bases inside the bubble
left flanking DNA-DNA base-pair columns (sense/antisense): C·G, A·T, T·A with dotted bonds
right flanking DNA-DNA base-pair columns (sense/antisense): G·C, A·T, C·G with dotted bonds
short vertical tick stems connecting each base letter to its ribbon
a movable transcription-position marker (RNA-polymerase cursor) along the template

interactions.label: Transcription position (mRNA length)
interactions.teaches: Dragging from 0 to 19 grows the magenta mRNA one complementary base at a time from its 5' end, each new base pairing to the next antisense template letter, so the learner sees RNA synthesized 5'→3' and reading the antisense (template) strand

interactions.label: Base-pairing view
interactions.teaches: Switching emphasis among the three pairing relationships makes complementarity explicit: DNA–DNA highlights the flanking double helix, DNA–RNA highlights template-to-transcript hydrogen bonds, and Sense vs mRNA lines up the two near-identical sequences to expose the T→U substitution

Hovering any exposed base reveals its paired partner and the 5'/3' direction of its strand, clarifying which strand is read as template (antisense, 3'→5') and which sequence the transcript matches (sense)

demo_steps.title: Transcription begins
demo_steps.narration: With the slider near 0 the bubble is open but the mRNA is just starting; the first U pairs to the antisense A at the 5' end of the transcript.

demo_steps.title: Elongation 5'→3'
demo_steps.narration: Advance the slider to ~10: the magenta strand has grown left-to-right, each base complementary to the cyan template, demonstrating directional synthesis.

demo_steps.title: Compare sense and mRNA
demo_steps.narration: At full length switch to 'Sense vs mRNA': the top blue-violet letters and the magenta letters align identically except every T on the sense strand is a U on the mRNA.

demo_steps.title: Double-helix flanks
demo_steps.narration: Switch to 'DNA–DNA' to emphasize the intact base pairs (C·G, A·T, T·A left; G·C, A·T, C·G right) that hold the helix together outside the open bubble.

interactionPlan.geometry_notes: Pure 2D front-on schematic, axis_screen_angles null. Lay bases on a horizontal grid: slot width ~0.5 world units, 25 slots total (3 left-flank + 19 bubble + 3 right-flank) spanning X ≈ [-6.25, +6.25]. Vertical layout: in the flanking regions sense ribbon at Y≈+0.7 and antisense at Y≈-0.7 (short dotted bonds between); through the bubble the sense ribbon bows up to Y≈+1.7 and antisense bows down to Y≈-1.7 (smooth cosine-like bow over the 19 bubble slots), with the mRNA ribbon flat at Y≈+0.15 inside the bubble only. Sense base letters sit just below the top ribbon (Y≈+1.1 in bubble), antisense letters just above the bottom ribbon (Y≈-1.1), mRNA letters just below the magenta ribbon (Y≈-0.25); dotted H-bond columns connect antisense↔mRNA letters in the bubble and sense↔antisense letters in the flanks. Colors: sense ribbon #5a6fb0 with darker letters #2a3a70; antisense ribbon #2fc0e6 with letters #0a7a96; mRNA ribbon #e0468c with letters #c01f6e; H-bond dots #444444; 5'/3' and name labels near-black #222222. Sequences — sense bubble: T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T; antisense bubble (complement): A G T C G A C C G A C T T G C G C A A; mRNA bubble (sense with U for T): U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U; left flank sense/antisense C·G, A·T, T·A; right flank G·C, A·T, C·G. The slider reveals mRNA bases index 0..(pos-1) and dims the not-yet-synthesized portion; the polymerase cursor sits at the boundary.
interactionPlan.notes: Build each ribbon as a flat extruded/rounded band (THREE.Shape or a thick line with rounded caps) following the bowed centerline; keep all geometry in the Z=0 plane and use an orthographic-style front camera so it reads as a textbook diagram. Render base letters as sprite/canvas textures or troika-text so they stay crisp and screen-aligned. Hydrogen bonds as small dotted LineSegments (3 dots per column). On slider change, toggle visibility/opacity of mRNA base sprites and their bond columns reactively and move the cursor marker. On toggle change, adjust emissive/opacity: emphasized pairs full color + bold bonds, others faded to ~0.25 opacity. Hover uses raycasting against invisible per-base hit planes to show a tooltip with the partner base and that strand's 5'→3' direction. No perspective depth needed; do not add orbit.

authoredContext:
Following formation of the polymerase–promoter complex, several turns of the DNA double helix untwist, forming a bubble and exposing 14 or so base pairs of the two strands. Appropriate ribonucleotides then line up by hydrogen-bonding to their complementary bases on DNA, bond formation occurs in the 5′ → 3′ direction, the RNA polymerase moves along the DNA chain, and the growing RNA molecule unwinds from DNA (the figure). At any one time, about 12 base pairs of the growing RNA remain hydrogen-bonded to the DNA template.

Biosynthesis of RNA using a DNA segment as a template.

Several turns of deoxyribonucleic acid double helix unwind exposing bases of the two strands. Ribonucleotides line up such that hydrogen bonds form in 5-prime to 3-prime direction.

Unlike what happens in DNA replication, where both strands are copied, only one of the two DNA strands is transcribed into mRNA. The DNA strand that contains the gene is often called the sense strand, or coding strand, and the DNA strand that gets transcribed to give RNA is called the antisense strand, or noncoding strand. Because the sense strand and the antisense strand in DNA are complementary, and because the DNA antisense strand and the newly formed RNA strand are also complementary, the RNA molecule produced during transcription is a copy of the DNA sense strand. That is, the complement of the complement is the same as the original. The only difference is that the RNA molecule has a U everywhere that the DNA sense strand has a T.

plan.authoredPrompt: This figure diagrams RNA transcription as a flat schematic of three nucleic acid strands drawn as tapered colored ribbons. A blue-violet ribbon runs across the top, labeled "DNA sense strand", marked 5' at its left tip and 3' at its right; a cyan ribbon runs along the bottom, labeled "DNA antisense strand", marked 3' at left and 5' at right. Both ribbons bow away from each other through the middle of the figure to open a bubble, and outside the bubble at each end their bases pair through vertical dot columns, C with G, A with T, and T with A at the left, G with C, A with T, and C with G at the right. Inside the bubble the sense strand's bases hang free and read T C A G C T G G C T G A A C G C G T T, while the antisense strand's exposed bases are hydrogen bonded to a magenta ribbon lying between the two, labeled "mRNA" by a leader line at its right end and marked 5' at left and 3' at right; its magenta bases read U C A G C U G G C U G A A C G C G U U. Placing the new transcript directly against its template makes the base-by-base complementarity readable in one glance, and comparing it upward with the blue-violet strand shows the two agree except that U stands wherever the sense strand carries T.
plan.authoredInteractions:
- Slider for transcription position: drag along the DNA template, and the open bubble advances while the magenta mRNA strand grows 5' to 3' with each new complementary base, showing how the antisense strand directs RNA synthesis.
- Toggle between base-pairing views: switch among DNA-DNA pairs, DNA-RNA pairs, and sense-vs-mRNA comparison, and the relevant hydrogen bonds or matching letters highlight, making complementarity and the T-to-U substitution clear.
- Hover for individual bases: hover over any exposed DNA or mRNA base, and its paired partner and strand direction labels appear, showing which strand is read and which sequence matches the transcript.
